about: Walking the Maze west of the Troll Room to the dead adventurer's remains: the loop that leads back to itself, one of the one-way tunnels down, the skeleton and what lies beside it, the sword's pulse at the rusty knife, a thing dropped to mark a room and seen there again among rooms all alike, and the way to the Cyclops closed in the Management's voice.

expect.words: West of House
You are standing in an open field west of a white house, with a boarded front door.
There is a small mailbox here.
North of House
You are facing the north side of a white house. There is no door here, and all the windows are boarded up. To the north a narrow path winds through the trees.
Behind House
You are behind the white house. A path leads into the forest to the east. In one corner of the house there is a small window which is slightly ajar.
With great effort, you open the window far enough to allow entry.
Kitchen

You are in the kitchen of the white house. A table seems to have been used recently for the preparation of food. A passage leads to the west and a dark staircase can be seen leading upward. A dark chimney leads down and to the east is a small window which is open.
On the table is an elongated brown sack, smelling of hot peppers.
A bottle is sitting on the table.
The glass bottle contains:
A quantity of water
Living Room

You are in the living room. There is a doorway to the east, a wooden door with strange gothic lettering to the west, which appears to be nailed shut, a trophy case, and a large oriental rug in the center of the room.
A battery-powered brass lantern is on the trophy case.
Above the trophy case hangs an elvish sword of great antiquity.
Taken.
Taken.
With a great effort, the rug is moved to one side of the room, revealing the dusty cover of a closed trap door.
The door reluctantly opens to reveal a rickety staircase descending into darkness.
The brass lantern is now on.
The trap door crashes shut, and you hear someone barring it.
Cellar
You are in a dark and damp cellar with a narrow passageway leading north, and a crawlway to the south. On the west is the bottom of a steep metal ramp which is unclimbable.
Your sword is glowing with a faint blue glow.
The Troll Room
This is a small room with passages to the east and south and a forbidding hole leading west. Bloodstains and deep scratches (perhaps made by an axe) mar the walls.
A nasty-looking troll, brandishing a bloody axe, blocks all passages out of the room.
Your sword has begun to glow very brightly.
(with the sword)
It's curtains for the troll as your sword removes his head.
Almost as soon as the troll breathes his last breath, a cloud of sinister black fog envelops him, and when the fog lifts, the carcass has disappeared.
Your sword is no longer glowing.

Maze
This is part of a maze of twisty little passages, all alike. A skeleton, probably the remains of a luckless adventurer, lies here.
The deceased adventurer's useless lantern is here.
Beside the skeleton is a rusty knife.
There is a skeleton key here.
An old leather bag, bulging with coins, is here.

The skeleton lies where its owner fell, slumped against the wall of the passage as though he had sat down for a moment's rest and found the moment longer than expected. It is picked quite clean, and has been for some time. Whatever he came into the maze looking for, the maze found him first.
It is a lantern of the old kind, rusted at every seam, its glass smoked black from the inside. Its batteries gave out some time before its owner did, which, down here, is the usual order of things.

It is a short knife, rusted nearly black, with a plain wooden grip worn smooth by a hand that is no longer in a position to hold it. The rust has not touched the edge. That is not a thing rust usually overlooks.

It is a heavy iron key, long in the shank, with a bow worked into the shape of a small grinning skull. Whatever lock it fits is a lock that wanted a key like this one, and is unlikely to be anywhere cheerful.
It is an old leather bag, cracked with age and drawn tight at the neck with a knotted thong, and it bulges in the way that only coins make a bag bulge. There are lots of coins in there.
There are lots of coins in there.
The coins are safely inside; there's no need to do that.
You can't turn that on.
It is already on.
As you touch the rusty knife, your sword gives a single pulse of blinding blue light.
Taken.
Taken.
Taken.

A sign is propped across the passage to the southeast: "CYCLOPS ROOM CLOSED UNTIL FURTHER NOTICE. Do not feed the cyclops. -- The Management." From somewhere beyond it comes a smell of old mutton and a snore like a rockslide. You decide the Management has a point.

A board is wedged across the passage to the southeast, lettered in the same patient hand as every other notice from the Management: "CYCLOPS ROOM CLOSED UNTIL FURTHER NOTICE. Do not feed the cyclops."

An old leather bag, bulging with coins, is here.

The passages are twisty, they are little, and they are all alike: the same rough walls, the same low ceiling, the same turnings that turn just far enough to hide where they are going. Whoever made this maze had one idea, and saw it through.
Your score is 35 (total of 350 points), in 42 moves.
This gives you the rank of Amateur Adventurer.
